claims.text: GitOps: desired state kept in Git, an agent pulls and applies it, deploying = a commit; agent inside the cluster is this course's setup, not the definition. Pull-based deployment: the agent reads desired state and changes its cluster, instead of an outside tool pushing.
claims.source_hint: content/glossary.yaml gitops, pull-based-deployment; OpenGitOps principles (declarative, versioned, pulled automatically, continuously reconciled); Argo CD docs: Core concepts / Overview

claims.text: deploy.sh@stage-2 lines 1-11: header says it runs on the host and kubectl talks to the kind cluster from there; 'Every step can run again'; first step kubectl apply -f deploy/k8s/namespace.yaml -o name.

deploy.sh@stage-2 builds Secrets from .env (scripts/k8s/secrets.sh, line 15) and deletes the previous Pod migrate before applying a new one (kubectl delete pod migrate -n donhang), so the credentials running it must allow creating Secrets and deleting Pods in donhang.
kubectl sends requests to the API server of the current context using the credentials of the user in the kubeconfig; kind adds a context kind-<name> for the cluster it creates.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Organizing cluster access using kubeconfig files; kind docs: Quick Start > Interacting with your cluster

claims.text: kubectl scale deployment/api -n donhang --replicas=1 changes spec.replicas stored in the cluster, so the Deployment keeps one Pod; nothing at stage-2 restores replicas: 2 from api.yaml, so it stays 1/1 until kubectl apply -f deploy/k8s/api.yaml sets it back to 2.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: kubectl scale; Declarative management of objects using configuration files (apply merge); examples/don-hang @ stage-2 (no controller of manifests in cluster)

claims.text: grep -n "replicas:" deploy/k8s/api.yaml at stage-2 prints one line: '11:  replicas: 2'. kubectl get deployment api -n donhang after scaling to 1 shows READY 1/1.
claims.source_hint: git -C examples/don-hang show stage-2:deploy/k8s/api.yaml | grep -n 'replicas:'; run on the stage-2 kind cluster

claims.text: In the course's setup a GitOps agent runs inside the cluster, reads the desired state from a Git repository and applies it through that cluster's API server; deploying a new version = committing a change (e.g. image: in api.yaml, by you or a CI job).
claims.source_hint: OpenGitOps principles; Argo CD docs: Overview > How it works

claims.text: The agent works as a control loop: it repeatedly compares the desired state in Git with the live objects it reads from its cluster's API server, so a hand-made difference is found at a later comparison without anyone running a command; whether it reverts it is configurable and taught later.
claims.source_hint: OpenGitOps principle 4 (continuously reconciled); Argo CD docs: Overview > How it works (continuously monitors, OutOfSync)

claims.text: kube-scheduler runs a control loop like the agent (as taught in k8s.l1.control-plane-components); OpenTofu does nothing between runs and finds drift only when a plan is run.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Concepts > Controllers; devops.l3.configuration-drift outline item 4; OpenTofu docs: plan (refresh)

claims.text: With pull, the in-cluster agent opens the connection outward to the Git repository, so nothing outside must reach the cluster's API server; CI needs write access to the repository and no longer holds cluster credentials.
claims.source_hint: OpenGitOps principles (pulled automatically); Argo CD docs: Security (repository credentials, in-cluster RBAC); Argo CD docs: repository polling vs webhooks

claims.text: Opinion: pull adds a component to install, upgrade and watch; for one small cluster that one person deploys, a push script run from CI can be enough (condition); when several people deploy or CI cannot reach the cluster, pull pays for that component (opposing context).
claims.source_hint: track.yaml outline item 6; Argo CD docs: Installation / Upgrading (component operated in the cluster)

claims.text: ci.yml@stage-2 lines 130-152: publish job, if push to master, needs [test, image], permissions: packages: write, downloads artifact images, docker load, logs in to ghcr.io with GITHUB_TOKEN.

No job in ci.yml@stage-2 deploys to a long-lived cluster: the k8s job creates a kind cluster on the runner (capture-output.sh --k8s) and deletes it with cluster-down.sh under if: always(); staging is a Compose run on the runner.
GitHub-hosted runners cannot reach a kind cluster on a developer's laptop (its API server listens on the local machine's loopback address by default in kind).
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Configuration > API Server (listenAddress default 127.0.0.1); GitHub Docs: About GitHub-hosted runners

claims.text: A secret used by a workflow (e.g. a kubeconfig) would be stored as a GitHub Actions secret in repository/environment settings.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Using secrets in GitHub Actions

claims.text: kubectl apply run by CI after every merge is push-based: it acts only when the pipeline runs and needs cluster credentials and network reach from the runner; it overwrites a hand-made change to a field in the manifest when it next applies that manifest.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Declarative management of objects using configuration files (how apply calculates differences)

claims.text: kubelet pulls images however manifests arrived; tag 1.0.0, no imagePullPolicy (IfNotPresent): a node pulls only if absent. kubectl describe pod lists Events (kept a limited time), incl. the pull. api.yaml@stage-2:22 ghcr.io/duyan11110/donhang-api:1.0.0.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Images (imagePullPolicy defaults); kubectl describe pod; examples/don-hang @ stage-2 deploy/k8s/api.yaml:22
